context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Stop serialising whole query results. Replace `res.json(utils.queryResultToJson(reviews))` with an explicit allow-list projection that returns only the fields the review listing needs (for example `id`, `rating`, `text`, `createdAt`, and a display name, if one is needed). Exclude personal data such as emails, internal user IDs, IP addresses, and other raw nested records. Put this projection in one shared function, such as `toReviewResponse(review)`, and call it from every route that returns review records, so all routes apply the same field limits. Where the requester is not entitled to a field, omit it based on their role or ownership, and add a test that checks the response contains only the allowed keys.
